chapter: Emmett Hardy and the river towns
title: Tom Brown, Brownlee and Abbie Brunies; meeting Emmett Hardy
summary: He recounts first playing with Brownlee and Abbie Brunies, then meeting Emmett Hardy at school in Gretna and forming a boys' band; Hardy died at 21 in 1925.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Speaking of Tom Brown, when was the first time you heard him or his band?

Tom, well, no, when, when, when I started, Tom was away. I didn't meet Tom till, till he came back to New Orleans, and the first time I played with Tom was with Brownlee's band, out at the old Spanish fort, and, and then, while I was, I think it was a couple of years after or before that, I was working with Abby Burns out at the halfway house, when his brother Theodore came down here, with a bunch of guys from Chicago, Murphy Steinberg, and, uh, was it Polo, Polo, Clarinet player, Danny Polo, Danny Polo, something like that. They were, they were, they had a band that they patterned off of the, off of the rhythm games. So, now, the, the, after, to follow up on that, that first job thing, after that, we moved from Harvard, we moved down to Gretton, and that's where I met Emmett Hardy, I went to school with, with Emmett, you see, and we formed a little band around Gretton, and he used to play across the river. We didn't get older than New Orleans, only on one job.
How old is Hardy? Was he older than you, or?
Uh, he was, no, he, he was, he was younger than me. Let's see, he died in, he died in 25, and he was 21 when he died.

Uh, but he covered a lot of ground in, in those years, and he used to make it, he made his own mop pieces. He, he worked in the, machine shop, and his, his, his brother, uh, today is head of this Bishop Edel machine company here, and he wanted him to be a machinist. Emmett didn't care about machinists, he, he wanted to play music. So he'd work all day in the fountain, and he made, he made his own mouth pieces. It was always experimenting, like Jack Teagarden, you know, always experimenting. I think he had a little engineer in him, frustrated engineer in him. And, uh, uh, uh, we had a little band over there, Sidney Arden, and, uh, Emmett, and Brownlee, and, uh, the kid that, that died at 16 years old was, would have been a marvelous trombone player by the name of Fort Myer. He had a brother who played cornet trumpet that you, you fellas, you might know of, Dick. He's from Jefferson, Paris. He played all these places along. Raymond talks about it. Yeah, Fort Myer. Fort Myer, they used to call him, but it's really Fort Myer. And, uh, he played beautiful from all. He had beautiful, uh, tones sort of like, like Santo, but better. Uh, you know, clearer, prettier. And he died when he was 16. And we were all just kids, and we played around, up and down, over the hill.
